quick.summary: How to find where users drop off by querying the people who quit.
quick.takeaway: Always keep the starting group in your data, even if they never finish.

beats.line: My query says everyone finished the flow. Why do I not believe it?
Because you are acting like a doctor checking only healthy people.
I matched the start events to the finish events.
And you threw away anyone who never finished.
In database terms, you did an inner join.
Can I just say matching only the winners?
Matching only the winners is spot on.
To find where people got stuck, you need the quitters too.
You have to keep the starting group, even without a match.
So I pull everyone who started, and leave blanks for the rest.
Now you can see where the pain really is.

quiz.question: You are querying data to find out why users abandon a checkout. What is the right approach?
options: Query everyone who started the checkout, keeping the non-buyers.
Query only the users who successfully bought an item.
Query the total count of page views.
Query only the users who clicked the final button.
quiz.explanation: To see where drop-offs happen, you must keep the entire starting group, even if the later events are blank.

quiz.question: Matching only the users who complete an action is a great way to find bottlenecks.
quiz.explanation: If you only look at people who succeeded, you throw away all the data about people who got stuck.
